summary: Product discharge conveyor motor stopped due to overload, causing product backlog.
details: The motor of the product discharge conveyor for hydraulic press #3 suddenly stopped after making an abnormal noise. Operator N confirmed that an unusually large amount of product had accumulated on the conveyor, causing the motor to overload. The motor's overload protection device activated, leading to the stoppage. The cause was a combination of excessive product supply from the previous process and reduced conveying capacity due to a slipping conveyor belt.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for conveyor motor restart and product tidying. Approximately 2 hours of production loss occurred. Concerns about impact on subsequent processes.
**Cost:** Motor repair was not required, but inspection costs were incurred.
causes: Excessive product supply from the previous process
Improper sensitivity setting of the overload protection device
immediate_actions: Shut down power to the press machine and conveyor.
Manually collect and organize accumulated products.
Adjust conveyor belt tension to eliminate slippage.
Reset the motor's overload protection device and attempt to restart.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After restarting, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Strengthen coordination with the previous process to thoroughly adjust product supply.
Add \"tension\" and \"wear condition\" to the conveyor belt's regular inspection items and clarify replacement criteria.
Review and adjust the sensitivity setting of the motor's overload protection device to an appropriate value.
Consider introducing a sensor to detect product accumulation on the conveyor.

summary: Product discharge conveyor guide rail damaged, causing products to fall and deform.
details: During the discharge of products pressed by hydraulic press #3 onto the product discharge conveyor, worker O discovered that a part of the guide rail on the side of the conveyor was damaged. Products passing through the damaged section fell off the guide rail onto the floor and were deformed. The damage is presumed to be due to metal fatigue caused by excessive force applied during a previous product jam.
impact_scope:
**Material Damage:** Approximately 10 fallen products were damaged and discarded. Rework is required.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was temporarily stopped for guide rail replacement and cleaning. Approximately 1.5 hours of production loss occurred. Slight delay in production schedule.
causes: Metal fatigue of guide rail (aging deterioration)
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine and identify the damaged guide rail.
Collect and count fallen and damaged products.
Immediately arrange for a replacement guide rail and perform the exchange.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After guide rail replacement, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Specifically add \"presence of cracks/deformation\" to the guide rail's regular inspection items and clarify check criteria.
Clearly state procedures for product jams in SOPs and re-educate workers not to apply excessive force.
Consider changing to a more durable guide rail material.
Consider installing a protective net or fall prevention fence under the conveyor.

summary: Product discharge conveyor chain broke, making conveyance impossible.
details: While the product discharge conveyor of hydraulic press #3 was operating, it suddenly stopped with a loud abnormal noise. Operator P confirmed that the conveyor's drive chain had broken. The breakage is presumed to be due to a combination of chain aging and wear due to insufficient lubrication. This completely stopped product conveyance.
impact_scope:
**Material Damage:** The drive chain broke and needs replacement. Minor impact on surrounding parts.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for chain replacement and adjustment. Approximately 4 hours of production loss occurred. Delay in production schedule.
causes: Aging deterioration of the drive chain
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine and shut off power.
Remove the broken chain and move it to a safe place.
Immediately begin arranging for a replacement chain and perform the exchange.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After chain replacement, adjust tension and lubricate, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"wear condition\" and \"lubrication condition\" to the drive chain's regular inspection items and clarify replacement criteria.
Clearly state lubrication frequency and procedures in SOPs and ensure thorough implementation.
Add chain tension adjustment to regular maintenance items.
Consider changing to a more durable chain material or introducing an automatic lubrication device.

summary: Product overlap and defects due to abnormal product discharge conveyor speed.
details: During the discharge of products pressed by hydraulic press #3 onto the product discharge conveyor, Inspector Q discovered that the conveyor's conveying speed was unstable. When the speed slowed down, products overlapped, resulting in numerous deformed defective products. The cause was found to be a malfunction of the conveyor's speed control inverter.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 30 products that overlapped due to abnormal speed were discarded as defective. Rework is required.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for inverter replacement and adjustment. Approximately 3 hours of production loss occurred. Delay in production schedule.
causes: Insufficient functional check of inverter during regular inspection
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine and isolate the defective lot.
Confirm inverter malfunction and immediately arrange for a replacement.
Replace the inverter and readjust speed settings.
Share status with relevant departments (Production Control, Quality Assurance).
After replacement, confirm speed stability with a test run and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"operation check\" and \"abnormality history check\" to the inverter's regular inspection items and clarify replacement criteria.
Secure spare inverter stock to enable quick replacement.
Consider introducing a system to monitor conveyor speed in real-time and alert in case of abnormality.
Increase inspection frequency of inverter cooling device.

summary: Product discharge conveyor chute jammed, causing product backflow.
details: A jam occurred in the chute section where products pressed by hydraulic press #3 are sent from the product discharge conveyor to the next process. Operator R confirmed that foreign matter was caught inside the chute, preventing smooth product flow and causing products to start flowing backward. This led to product accumulation on the conveyor and automatic stoppage of the press machine. The foreign matter was found to be a small part that fell during previous maintenance.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for chute jam resolution and product tidying. Approximately 2 hours of production loss occurred. Concerns about impact on subsequent processes.
**Cost:** Minor material damage. Labor costs for cleaning work incurred.
causes: Foreign matter ingress into chute (fallen object during maintenance)
immediate_actions: Shut down power to the press machine and conveyor.
Remove foreign matter from inside the chute and clear the jam.
Manually collect and organize accumulated products.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After cleaning, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Strengthen foreign matter fall prevention measures during maintenance and ensure thorough cleaning and checking after work.
Add \"presence of foreign matter\" and \"signs of jam\" to the chute's daily inspection items.
Review chute shape and consider improving it to a less jam-prone structure.
Consider introducing a foreign matter detection sensor at the chute entrance.

summary: Finger caught during product discharge conveyor cleaning, resulting in minor injury.
details: During cleaning of the product discharge conveyor of hydraulic press #3, worker S's finger was caught in the conveyor's drive unit, resulting in a bruise. The cause was the conveyor unexpectedly operating without power being shut off during cleaning. Non-compliance with safety procedures and insufficient hazard prediction activities before work were pointed out.
impact_scope:
**Personal Injury:** Worker S sustained a bruised finger. Diagnosis at the hospital indicated a full recovery in 1 week. Currently on leave.
**Impact on Production:** Cleaning work interrupted. One other worker temporarily left work to accompany the injured worker to the infirmary. Press machine operation delayed by approximately 1 hour.
causes: Non-compliance with safety procedures (insufficient power shutdown)
Insufficient hazard prediction activities before work
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine and shut off power.
Provide first aid to the injured person and transport to the infirmary.
Protect the scene and take photographs.
Conduct initial investigation by interviewing relevant personnel.
Report to superiors.
Temporarily suspend cleaning work.
permanent_actions: Revise cleaning work SOP to include power shutdown (LOTO) procedures and safety checks, and create video manuals.
Conduct re-education for all workers using the revised SOP and video manuals.
Mandate hazard prediction training (KYT) for cleaning work.
Consider installing a safety cover on the conveyor drive unit.

summary: Product discharge conveyor bearing seized, abnormal noise and stoppage.
details: An abnormal friction noise occurred from the roller section of the product discharge conveyor of hydraulic press #3. Operator T confirmed that the roller's bearing had overheated and seized. This made roller rotation difficult and stopped the conveyor. The cause was insufficient bearing lubrication and overlooking the regular replacement timing.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for bearing replacement and adjustment. Approximately 3 hours of production loss occurred. Concerns about impact on subsequent processes.
**Cost:** Bearing replacement costs and parts costs incurred.
causes: Delay in early detection of abnormal noise
immediate_actions: Shut down power to the press machine and conveyor.
Identify the seized bearing and begin replacement work.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After bearing replacement, lubricate, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Clarify regular bearing lubrication and replacement cycles and state them in SOPs.
Optimize the type and amount of lubricant.
Consider introducing a sensor to detect abnormal noise and build an early alert system.
Conduct training for workers to detect and report abnormal equipment noises early.

summary: Products slipped on the inclined section of the product discharge conveyor, causing a jam.
details: On the inclined section of the product discharge conveyor of hydraulic press #3, products slipped and jammed at the bottom. Worker U confirmed that the conveyor belt surface was worn, reducing friction with the products. This caused products to slide down without being able to climb the incline, colliding with subsequent products and jamming.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for jam resolution and product tidying. Approximately 1.5 hours of production loss occurred. Concerns about impact on subsequent processes.
**Cost:** Minor material damage. Labor costs for cleaning work incurred.
causes: Overlooking belt wear during daily inspection
immediate_actions: Shut down power to the press machine and conveyor.
Remove jammed products and organize them.
Check the wear condition of the conveyor belt.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After cleaning, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"surface wear condition\" to the conveyor belt's regular inspection items and clarify replacement criteria.
Consider changing to a high-friction belt suitable for inclined conveyance.
Consider introducing a sensor to detect product slippage on the inclined section.
Consider installing a belt cleaner to maintain the cleanliness of the belt surface.

summary: Product surface scratches due to product discharge conveyor vibration.
details: During the discharge of products pressed by hydraulic press #3 onto the product discharge conveyor, Inspector V discovered that products were contacting each other and getting scratched on the surface due to abnormal conveyor vibration. The line was immediately stopped, and upon inspection, it was found that the conveyor frame fixing bolts were loose, making the entire structure unstable.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 40 products with surface scratches due to vibration were discarded as defective. Rework is required.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for tightening and adjustment of frame fixing bolts. Approximately 2 hours of production loss occurred. Delay in production schedule.
causes: Insufficient bolt tightening check during regular inspection
Delay in early detection of abnormal vibration
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine and isolate the defective lot.
Check all conveyor frame fixing bolts and retighten loose ones.
Share status with relevant departments (Production Control, Quality Assurance).
After retightening, confirm vibration stability with a test run and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"tightening torque check\" to the conveyor frame fixing bolt's regular inspection items and strictly record it.
Consider introducing anti-loosening nuts or washers.
Consider introducing a sensor to detect abnormal vibration and build an early alert system.
Conduct training for workers to detect and report abnormal equipment vibrations early.

summary: Product discharge conveyor control panel short-circuited, all functions stopped.
details: While the product discharge conveyor of hydraulic press #3 was operating, smoke suddenly came from the control panel, and all conveyor functions stopped. Operator W confirmed that wiring inside the control panel had short-circuited, and the breaker had tripped. The cause was found to be insulation failure due to moisture ingress into the control panel.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for control panel repair and replacement. Approximately 5 hours of production loss occurred. Significant delay in production schedule.
**Cost:** Control panel repair or replacement costs incurred.
causes: Insufficient waterproofing/moisture-proofing measures for control panel
Insufficient internal control panel check during regular inspection
immediate_actions: Shut down power to the press machine and conveyor.
Identify the short-circuited area inside the control panel and begin repair or replacement work.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After repair or replacement, perform power-on test and functional check and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Strengthen waterproofing/moisture-proofing measures for the control panel and review installation environment.
Add \"presence of moisture/condensation\" and \"insulation condition of wiring\" to the control panel's regular internal inspection items.
Increase cleaning frequency of control panel cooling fan filter.
Secure spare control panel stock to enable quick replacement.

summary: Burrs occurred on pressed products, many judged as defective, leading to production stoppage.
details: During the pressing of product A on hydraulic press #3, Inspector B discovered burrs exceeding the specified limit on products discharged during an intermediate inspection. The line was immediately stopped, and upon checking the current situation, a minute crack was found at the tip of the die (upper die). This caused pressure leakage and material overflow during molding.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 500 units (2 hours' worth) of product A produced during pressing were all discarded as defective. Concerns arose about delays in delivery to customers.
**Impact on Production:** Hydraulic press #3 operation stopped for approximately 4 hours for die replacement and adjustment. Impact on subsequent processes also occurred.
causes: Fatigue crack in die (upper die) (aging deterioration)
Overlooking cracks during regular die inspection
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine and isolate the defective lot.
Immediately replace the die (upper die).
Conduct 100% inspection to identify the range of defective products.
Perform test shots with the replaced die and confirm quality.
Share status with relevant departments (Production Control, Quality Assurance).
permanent_actions: Review die regular maintenance standards and add more detailed check items for wear and fatigue conditions.
Consider introducing non-destructive testing (e.g., penetrant testing) for areas prone to cracking.
Establish replacement criteria based on die usage count and thoroughly manage its lifespan.
Strengthen quality check steps during die replacement.

summary: Press machine operated with insufficient die (upper die) clamping, damaging the die.
details: After morning setup work on hydraulic press #3, Operator C began the start-up inspection. Without noticing that the die (upper die) air clamp was not fixed with sufficient pressure, the press was started. During the first press cycle, the die shifted slightly, and as a result, the joint part of the upper die was damaged.
impact_scope:
**Material Damage:** The die (upper die) was damaged and requires repair or new fabrication. Costs are being estimated but are expected to be high.
**Impact on Production:** Hydraulic press #3 immediately stopped due to die damage. Production may be stopped for up to approximately 1 week until a replacement die becomes available in the manufacturing department. Significant delay in production schedule.
causes: Air clamp mechanism pressure drop (equipment malfunction)
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine.
Remove the damaged die and move it to a safe place.
Check the pressure gauge of the air clamp mechanism.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
Temporarily suspend press machine restart.
Begin preparing a replacement die.
permanent_actions: Introduce an air clamp pressure monitoring system and strengthen the interlock function to prevent the press machine from starting if the pressure is below the specified value.
Add pressure gauge value check and double-check items after die clamping to the setup work checklist.
Conduct re-education for workers on safety check procedures during setup work.
Increase the frequency of regular maintenance of the air clamp system and inspection of the pressure relief valve.

summary: Product discharge conveyor belt damaged, causing products to fall and break.
details: During the discharge of products pressed by hydraulic press #3 onto the product discharge conveyor, a crack was found in a part of the conveyor belt. Products caught in this crack fell off the side of the conveyor and were damaged. The fallen products were molded parts and were deformed by the impact, rendering them unusable. The crack was minute, caused by previous foreign matter ingress, and was not detected during daily inspection.
impact_scope:
**Material Damage:** Approximately 5 fallen products were damaged and discarded. Rework is required.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was temporarily stopped for emergency conveyor belt replacement and cleaning. Approximately 1.5 hours of production loss occurred. Slight delay in production schedule.
causes: Aging deterioration of conveyor belt and overlooking minute cracks
Insufficient visual inspection during daily inspection
Ambiguity in criteria for evaluating deterioration status
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine and identify the damaged part of the conveyor belt.
Collect and count fallen and damaged products.
Immediately begin arranging for a replacement conveyor belt and perform the exchange.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After conveyor replacement, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Specifically add \"presence of minute cracks/damage\" to the conveyor belt's daily inspection items and clarify check criteria.
Mandate full circumference inspection of the conveyor during regular inspection and consider introducing wear gauges or crack detection tools.
Consider installing a protective net or fall prevention fence under the conveyor.
Strengthen quality checks during belt replacement.

summary: Product discharge conveyor drive motor stopped, causing product backlog.
details: While hydraulic press #3 was operating, an abnormal noise occurred from the product discharge conveyor drive unit, and then the motor stopped. Discharged products began to accumulate on the conveyor, eventually making product discharge from the press machine impossible, and the press machine automatically stopped due to a safety interlock. The motor's internal bearing had overheated and seized.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for conveyor motor repair and product collection/tidying. Approximately 3 hours of production loss occurred. Concerns about impact on subsequent processes.
**Cost:** Motor repair costs (bearing replacement) and parts costs incurred.
causes: Insufficient regular maintenance of drive motor (overlooking bearing replacement timing)
Insufficient worker awareness of initial abnormal noise from drive unit
immediate_actions: Shut down power to the press machine and conveyor.
Manually collect and organize accumulated products.
Inspect the drive motor and identify the cause of failure.
Arrange for a repair technician and perform bearing replacement work.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After repair completion, confirm functionality and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Formulate a preventive maintenance plan for the conveyor drive motor and clarify the regular bearing replacement cycle.
Consider introducing a sensor to detect abnormal noise or vibration from the drive unit and build a system to alert in case of abnormality.
Conduct training for workers to detect and report abnormal equipment noises or smells early.
Secure spare stock of important drive components.

summary: Press machine frequently stopped due to product discharge conveyor sensor malfunction.
details: During product production on hydraulic press #3, the \"product passage detection sensor\" installed on the product discharge conveyor frequently malfunctioned, incorrectly detecting \"no passage\" even when products were actually passing. This caused the press machine's safety interlock to activate, repeatedly stopping production at short intervals. The cause was found to be dust adhering to the sensor lens.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** Repeated short-term stoppages due to sensor malfunction resulted in a total of approximately 2 hours of production loss. Production efficiency significantly decreased.
**Cost:** Labor costs for sensor cleaning incurred. No parts replacement required.
causes: Contamination of product passage detection sensor (dust adhesion)
Insufficient daily inspection items for sensor cleaning
Inadequate sensor installation environment (insufficient dust protection)
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine.
Check the lens of the product passage detection sensor and clean off adhering dust.
Readjust sensor sensitivity and confirm normal operation.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After sensor operation confirmation, resume production.
permanent_actions: Clearly state daily cleaning of the product passage detection sensor in work procedures and ensure thorough implementation.
Increase cleaning frequency around sensor installation locations and strengthen dust protection measures (e.g., install dust covers, consider air curtains).
Review sensor sensitivity setting criteria and consider settings robust to environmental changes.
Consider optimizing sensor mounting angle and position.

summary: Product dimensional accuracy decreased due to die (upper die) wear, causing defective products.
details: During the pressing of product A on hydraulic press #3, Inspector X discovered that the product's dimensions were slightly smaller than the specified value. The line was immediately stopped, and upon checking, it was found that the molding part of the die (upper die) was worn. This caused uneven pressure during molding, leading to a decrease in dimensional accuracy.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 100 products with dimensional accuracy defects were discarded as defective. Concerns arose about delays in delivery to customers.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for die replacement and adjustment. Approximately 4 hours of production loss occurred. Impact on subsequent processes also occurred.
causes: Overlooking wear during regular die inspection
immediate_actions: Stop the press machine and isolate the defective lot.
Immediately replace the die (upper die).
Conduct 100% inspection to identify the range of defective products.
Perform test shots with the replaced die and confirm quality.
Share status with relevant departments (Production Control, Quality Assurance).
permanent_actions: Review die regular maintenance standards and add more detailed check items for wear condition.
Establish replacement criteria based on die usage count and thoroughly manage its lifespan.
Strengthen quality check steps during die replacement.
Consider introducing an in-line inspection device for real-time dimension measurement.

summary: Product thermal deformation due to die (upper die) cooling water leakage.
details: During the pressing of product A on hydraulic press #3, Operator Y discovered that thermal deformation was occurring in the product. Upon checking, it was found that cooling water was leaking from the cooling water piping of the die (upper die), and the die was not sufficiently cooled. This caused the product to undergo thermal deformation when separating from the die.
impact_scope:
**Material Damage:** The cooling water piping of the die (upper die) was damaged and requires repair. Costs are minor.
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for cooling water piping repair and die temperature adjustment. Approximately 2 hours of production loss occurred. Delay in production schedule.
causes: Deterioration of die (upper die) cooling water piping
Overlooking water leakage during regular inspection
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine.
Identify the cooling water piping leakage point and perform repair.
Cool the die to the specified temperature.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After repair, confirm cooling function with a test run and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"presence of water leakage\" and \"deterioration condition of piping\" to the cooling water piping's regular inspection items.
Consider introducing a sensor to monitor cooling water flow rate/temperature and build a system to alert in case of abnormality.
Review cooling water management standards and thoroughly manage water quality.
Consider changing to a more durable piping material.

summary: Foreign matter caught between die (upper die) and lower die, causing product jam.
details: During the pressing of product A on hydraulic press #3, worker Z noticed that the press machine's operation was heavy and stopped it. Upon checking, a small metal piece was caught between the die (upper die) and the lower die, causing products to jam without being fully formed. The foreign matter was found to be a part of a component that fell during a previous die change.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for foreign matter removal and die cleaning. Approximately 1.5 hours of production loss occurred. Concerns about impact on subsequent processes.
**Cost:** Minor material damage. Labor costs for cleaning work incurred.
causes: Foreign matter fall during die change
Insufficient cleaning and checking after die change
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine and shut off power.
Remove foreign matter between dies and clean the die.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After cleaning, confirm die operation with a test run and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Strengthen foreign matter fall prevention measures during die change and ensure thorough cleaning and checking after work.
Add \"presence of foreign matter\" and \"die clearance check\" to the checklist after die change.
Increase cleaning frequency around the die.
Consider introducing a foreign matter detection sensor between dies.

summary: Finger caught during die (upper die) adjustment, resulting in minor injury.
details: During fine adjustment of the die (upper die) of hydraulic press #3, worker AA's finger was caught when the die unexpectedly moved, resulting in a bruise. The cause was neglecting to insert the safety pin during adjustment work, leaving the die unfixed. Non-compliance with safety procedures and insufficient hazard prediction activities before work were pointed out.
impact_scope:
**Personal Injury:** Worker AA sustained a bruised finger. Diagnosis at the hospital indicated a full recovery in 1 week. Currently on leave.
**Impact on Production:** Adjustment work interrupted. One other worker temporarily left work to accompany the injured worker to the infirmary. Press machine operation delayed by approximately 1 hour.
causes: Non-compliance with safety procedures (insufficient safety pin insertion)
Insufficient hazard prediction activities before work
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine and shut off power.
Provide first aid to the injured person and transport to the infirmary.
Protect the scene and take photographs.
Conduct initial investigation by interviewing relevant personnel.
Report to superiors.
Temporarily suspend die adjustment work.
permanent_actions: Revise die adjustment SOP to include safety pin insertion procedures and safety checks, and create video manuals.
Conduct re-education for all workers using the revised SOP and video manuals.
Mandate hazard prediction training (KYT) for die adjustment work.
Consider strengthening the interlock of the die fixing mechanism.

summary: Die (upper die) heater malfunction, causing product molding defects.
details: During the pressing of product A on hydraulic press #3, Operator BB noticed that the product's molding condition was unstable and stopped it. Upon checking, it was found that a part of the heater built into the die (upper die) was malfunctioning, and the die was not heated to the specified temperature. This caused poor material fluidity and molding defects.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The press machine was emergency stopped for heater replacement and die temperature adjustment. Approximately 3 hours of production loss occurred. Delay in production schedule.
**Cost:** Heater replacement costs and parts costs incurred.
causes: Insufficient functional check of heater during regular inspection
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the press machine.
Identify the malfunctioning heater and begin replacement work.
Heat the die to the specified temperature.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After heater replacement, confirm temperature stability with a test run and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"resistance value measurement\" and \"power continuity check\" to the die heater's regular inspection items and clarify replacement criteria.
Consider introducing a system to monitor die temperature in real-time and alert in case of abnormality.
Secure spare heater stock to enable quick replacement.
Increase inspection frequency of heater wiring and connections.

summary: Numerous welding defects due to welding torch malfunction, leading to production stoppage.
details: During welding of product B on welding robot system #1, Operator J noticed that the weld bead shape was unstable and stopped the machine. Upon checking, it was found that spatter frequently accumulated inside the welding torch nozzle, causing arc instability. This resulted in numerous welding defects such as spatter inclusion and poor groove even with normal current and voltage settings.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 50 products with unstable weld beads were discarded as defective. Concerns arose about delays in delivery to customers.
**Impact on Production:** The welding robot system was temporarily stopped for welding torch maintenance and adjustment. Approximately 2 hours of production loss occurred.
causes: Decreased performance of spatter removal function (e.g., air blow)
Mismatch between welding conditions and consumable selection
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the robot system.
Disassemble the welding torch and thoroughly remove spatter from inside the nozzle.
Check torch consumables (tips, nozzles, etc.) and replace heavily worn ones.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
Fine-tune welding conditions and confirm quality with test welding.
permanent_actions: Increase inspection frequency of welding torch's automatic spatter removal function and readjust air blow pressure/flow rate.
Consider changing to a nozzle shape or material less prone to spatter adhesion.
Clearly state torch cleaning work before welding and at regular intervals in work procedures and ensure thorough implementation.
Review welding conditions (gas flow rate, wire stick-out, etc.) and improve to suppress spatter generation.

summary: Welding position shifted due to welding robot program error, causing defective products.
details: During welding of product B on welding robot system #1, Inspector M discovered that the weld bead was shifted several millimeters from its intended position. The line was immediately stopped, and upon checking, it was found that an incorrect offset value had been entered during a program modification the previous day, preventing the robot from accurately tracing the specified weld path. This resulted in numerous defective products with insufficient weld strength.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 80 products with shifted welding positions were discarded as defective. Concerns arose about delays in delivery to customers.
**Impact on Production:** The welding robot system was temporarily stopped for program modification and test welding. Approximately 3 hours of production loss occurred.
causes: Insufficient operation check after program modification
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the robot system and isolate the defective lot.
Correct the program offset value and set the correct weld path.
Perform test welding with the modified program and confirm quality.
Share status with relevant departments (Production Control, Quality Assurance, Engineering Department).
permanent_actions: Strictly enforce robot program change management procedures and mandate double-checking and test welding after changes.
Record program change history in detail and clarify change content and approvers.
Strengthen cooperation between offline teaching system and online teaching to reduce human error.
Consider introducing a sensor to monitor welding quality in real-time.

summary: Welding torch cooling water leaked, causing arc instability.
details: During welding of product B on welding robot system #1, Operator CC discovered that water was leaking from the welding torch. This caused arc instability and uneven weld beads. Upon checking, a crack was found in the cooling water hose inside the torch, and cooling water was leaking. Overheating of the torch also occurred due to insufficient cooling.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Production:** The welding robot system was emergency stopped for cooling water hose replacement and torch temperature adjustment. Approximately 2.5 hours of production loss occurred.
**Cost:** Cooling water hose replacement costs and parts costs incurred.
causes: Deterioration of cooling water hose (aging deterioration)
Overlooking water leakage during regular inspection
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the robot system.
Identify the cooling water hose leakage point and perform replacement.
Cool the torch to the specified temperature.
Report to relevant personnel and superiors.
After replacement, confirm cooling function and arc stability with a test run and resume operation.
permanent_actions: Add \"presence of water leakage\" and \"deterioration condition of hose\" to the cooling water hose's regular inspection items.
Consider introducing a sensor to monitor cooling water flow rate/temperature and build a system to alert in case of abnormality.
Review cooling water management standards and thoroughly manage water quality.
Consider changing to a more durable hose material.

summary: Numerous welding defects due to worn welding torch electrode tip.
details: During welding of product B on welding robot system #1, Inspector DD noticed that the weld bead shape was rough and there was a lot of spatter, and stopped the machine. Upon checking, it was found that the welding torch electrode tip was significantly worn. This caused the arc to not concentrate, leading to a decrease in welding quality. The cause was that the tip replacement timing had passed.
impact_scope:
**Impact on Quality:** Approximately 60 products with welding defects were discarded as defective. Concerns arose about delays in delivery to customers.
**Impact on Production:** The welding robot system was temporarily stopped for electrode tip replacement and adjustment. Approximately 1.5 hours of production loss occurred.
causes: Insufficient compatibility between welding conditions and tip
immediate_actions: Emergency stop the robot system.
Immediately replace the worn electrode tip.
Fine-tune welding conditions and confirm quality with test welding.
Share status with relevant departments (Production Control, Quality Assurance).
permanent_actions: Clarify regular electrode tip replacement cycle and state it in SOPs.
Consider introducing a sensor to monitor tip wear condition in real-time.
Review optimal tip selection criteria according to welding conditions.
Strengthen quality check steps during tip replacement.

summary: Welding torch cable disconnected, no arc generated.
details: During welding of product B on welding robot system #1, Operator EE attempted to start welding but noticed that no arc was generated. Upon checking, it was found that a part of the cable connected to the welding torch was disconnected. The disconnection was due to a combination of repetitive stress from robot arm movement and insufficient cable protection.
impact_scope:
**Material Damage:** Welding torch cable disconnected and needs replacement. Costs are moderate.
**Impact on Production:** The welding robot system was emergency stopped for cable replacement and adjustment. Approximately 3 hours of production loss occurred. Delay in production schedule.
causes: Disconnection of welding torch cable (metal fatigue)
Overlooking cable deterioration during regular inspection
